segments.title: The short, and the same test
sections: The Short At The Top Of The Range

cues.text: You know this one. Price runs up into the prior-day high, a level, a price you marked before the session.
It pokes four points through, stalls, and looks like the top, so you sell it.
The next five-minute bar closes above the zone, the band of prices around the level, then the one after, and your stop fills.
In the next session the same poke comes. This time you wait, and price drops forty points without you.
The poke was the same both times. The answer was not, and the short never got the memo.
Both sessions asked one question: does price hold at the level, or fail?
Now, the test.
Held, that is acceptance: a 5-minute close beyond the zone, within 15 minutes of the first touch. That is Module 10.
Failed, that is rejection, this module: the same test with the other answer.
It is a setup, a location plus a read, and the read is context.
It carries no entry of its own.
The example.
The prior-day value area high, pd-vah, the short name you log it under, is a zone from 24,500 to 24,505.
Price arrives from below, so the far edge, the side furthest from where price came, is 24,505.
First touch at 9:52 a.m. That starts a 15-minute window, which ends at 10:07.
The 5-minute bars close at 24,503, 24,499 and 24,488. None closed above 24,505.
A close at 24,509 would have been acceptance, and the read would belong to Module 10.
At 10:07 the window has passed and price is below the zone. That is a rejection.
The rule:
A rejection is called only at a range extreme: a level on your list that bounds a range, like the prior-day high and low, the value area high and low, or the overnight high and low.
It is called once the 15 minutes have passed with no 5-minute close beyond the far edge, and only with price back on the range side of the zone. Until then the read is open.
Getting it wrong is…
Writing rejected at 9:54, two minutes after the touch, because a bar left a wick. You want the answer before the bars have given it.
The fix: at the first touch, write the window's end time beside the zone.
Pd-vah, first touch 9:52, window ends 10:07. No read goes in your notes before that time.

options: Price tested the extreme and was not accepted beyond it
check.why: A rejection is the acceptance test with the other answer: no 5-minute close beyond the zone inside the window, and price back on the range side. It is a context read.

Never, a close would be needed

segments.title: What a rejection does, and the failed breakdown
sections: What A Rejection Does To Your Plan
The Failed Breakdown: Two Closes, Then A Reclaim

cues.text: A rejection changes your plan in one of three ways. None of them is an order.
One: it cancels a branch. A branch is one if-then line of your plan, and one that needed acceptance at this zone does not switch on.
Two: it ends a branch. A branch live on acceptance ends when price closes back through its invalidation, the close you wrote down before.
Three: it sets a target: the extreme that just held, for a branch trading back toward it.
The rule:
A rejection cancels a branch, ends a branch or sets a target. It never places an order.
Getting it wrong is a short at 10:07, the minute the window closed. That turns a context read into a trigger, and the trade is No Setup, the tag for a trade with no branch.
The fix is one line in your session notes: pd-vah, test 1, the first test of that level this session, rejected 10:07, branch 1 cancelled.
Writing that line is the whole action. There is no order ticket attached, and no slippage on a sentence.
Now, the one failure this course does trade.
Part one: at least two 1-minute closes beyond the far edge. A sweep, a quick move through the stops resting at a level, is only a print.
Part two: a 1-minute close back through the whole zone, beyond its near edge, the side price came from. That is the reclaim.
Below a level, that is a failed breakdown, and the trade, if its trigger fires, is long.
Above a level, it is a failed breakout, and the trade is short.
The example. The on-low, the overnight low, is a zone from 24,290 to 24,296.
Price comes down from above, so the near edge is 24,296 and the far edge is 24,290.
At 10:31 a 1-minute bar closes at 24,286, below the far edge: close one.
At 10:32 the next closes at 24,281: close two.
At 10:33 a bar closes at 24,299, above the near edge: the reclaim.
The rule:
The read needs both parts, in order. The sweep alone is not a trade.
Getting it wrong is a buy inside the sweep bar at 10:31 because the stops below are being run. That is a story about other people's stops, not a read of the level.
The fix: three boxes on the plan line. Close one, close two, reclaim. No ticket until all three are ticked.

cues.text: The reclaim tells you the breakdown failed. It does not tell you to enter.
The trigger is Pause N Go, from Module 13, fired from the zone price has just reclaimed. Pause: at least two 1-minute bars hold inside it.
Continue the on-low example. At 10:35 price pulls back and trades 24,295, the first touch of the zone after the reclaim.
The 10:36 and 10:37 bars trade entirely inside the zone, with no close below 24,290. That is the pause. Two bars. It is the shortest wait in the course, and it will feel like an hour.
At 10:38 a bar closes at 24,299, above the pause high of 24,296. That is the resumption, and that close is the entry.
The stop rests behind the far edge, at 24,288, two points below 24,290.
Now, the branch. Every trade in the course comes from a line you wrote before 9:25.
One: if price prints two 1-minute closes below the on-low zone.
Two: then a 1-minute close back above its near edge, and a Pause N Go fires from the reclaimed zone.
Three: then the target, which is a level.
Four: the invalidation, the close that ends the branch, is a 5-minute close below 24,290, before or after the reclaim.
The construction comes at the trigger, from Module 14: the stop behind the far edge, and the 2 to 1 check, the target at least twice as far as the stop.
Then the size, from the stop distance and the grade, A-plus down to C.
The rule:
The only entry this page teaches is Pause N Go from the reclaimed zone, off a branch written before 9:25, with the stop resting behind the far edge.
No Pause N Go, no trade. The read stays context.
If the pause fails, with a close below 24,290, there is no trigger and no trade. If the trigger fires and the stop fills, that was a planned trade that lost, with no negative tag.
Getting it wrong is a buy on the close of the reclaim bar at 10:33. That skips the one thing the pause exists to show: whether price can hold the reclaimed zone at all.
The fix: leave the order ticket unarmed until both pause bars have closed.
Then write the trigger's price condition on the plan line, 1-minute close above 24,296, and arm the order only when that line is true.

segments.title: Trapped Traders, and the pull to sell the top
sections: Trapped Traders Confirms; It Doesn't Trigger
The Pull To Sell The Top

cues.text: Trapped Traders are traders holding positions price has just moved against, like buyers of a breakout that fell back inside the range.
On a footprint chart, which shows the orders traded at each price, Module 7 gives the signature three parts.
One: stacked imbalances at the extreme, a run of prices where one side was far heavier.
Two: the next bar closes back through the level.
Three: delta, buyers minus sellers, flips to the other side.
On the on-low example the 10:32 bar had three stacked selling imbalances and a delta of minus 240. The 10:33 bar closed back above 24,296 with plus 205. All three boxes ticked.
The rule:
Trapped Traders confirms a failed breakdown or breakout read already on the chart. It is recorded in the journal's confirmation field, never acted on, and it never changes size.
Getting it wrong is a second contract added because trapped printed and this one is cleaner. That turns the footprint into reassurance, and reassurance leaks into size.
The fix: fill the size line from the stop distance and the grade before you open the footprint panel. The footprint can add a word, never a number.
Now, the pull to sell the top. A range invites certainty.
By the third test it feels like a pattern, and selling there feels like reading the market. Mostly it is wanting to have called the turn.
The rejection read is sometimes right, and that is enough to feel like a signal. A read that is sometimes right is the most expensive kind. It feels right all the time.
A context read that fails costs you nothing. A fade with no trigger that fails costs you R, the amount you risked, and a tag.
The rule:

At a range extreme, the only orders are the ones a written branch names: acceptance and a trigger, or the failed breakdown or breakout read and its Pause N Go. Everything else is the nothing case: no order.
Getting it wrong is a resting sell limit at the pd-high, the prior-day high, before the open because it rejected in the prior session. The journal records trigger none.
The fix: before 9:25, every range-extreme zone on your pre-market sheet carries one word, a branch number or nothing. A nothing zone gets its two alerts, near edge and far edge, and never an order.
When it rejects in the session, say aloud: rejected, branch cancelled. Then write the session-notes line.

cues.text: Two hypothetical illustrations, not trade records: composite sessions, invented prices. Case 1: the pd-val zone, the prior-day value area low, runs 24,376 to 24,382, with price above it and falling.
The branch, written before 9:25, targets the pd-vpoc, the prior-day volume point of control, at 24,440.
At 10:16 and 10:17 two 1-minute closes print below the far edge, 24,376.
At 10:18 a bar closes at 24,385, back above the near edge: the reclaim. Trapped Traders prints, all three boxes.
No 5-minute close printed below the zone, so the invalidation never fired.
Price pulls back. Two bars hold inside the zone, and at 10:23 a close at 24,386 is the go.
Construction. Entry is 24,386, on the 10:23 close.
The stop rests at 24,374, two points behind the far edge: 12 points, 48 ticks.
The target, the pd-vpoc, is 54 points away. That is 4.5 to 1, which clears the 2 to 1 check.
The four grade checks: named level, yes. Trigger before entry, yes.
Stop behind structure, yes. Size matched the plan, yes. A-plus, from the plan, not the outcome.
Case 2, a different composite. The pd-high zone runs 25,118 to 25,124.
Price is below it, so the far edge is 25,124. Branch 1 needs acceptance above it. The plan has no failed breakout branch here, so that read sits in the nothing case.
At 10:06, the first touch: beside the zone you write, first touch 10:06, window ends 10:21.
At 10:07 a 1-minute bar closes at 25,127, then the next closes back inside at 25,121. One close beyond, not two.
The 5-minute bars close at 25,122, 25,109 and 25,101. None above 25,124.
At 10:21 the window has passed: a rejection. Branch 1 is cancelled for test 1.
The line: pd-high, test 1, rejected 10:21, branch 1 cancelled. Later price reaches the pd-vpoc, but the plan had no order for that move: no trade, no grade.
What the two cases share.
Both rejections were decided by closed bars at times written on the chart. In Case 1 a reclaim, a trigger and a written branch made a trade. In Case 2 a failure alone changed the plan.
The rule: the branch you wrote before 9:25 decided which case was a trade. Both charts looked equally sure of themselves, which is what charts do.
Getting it wrong is calling Case 2 a missed trade. It was a branch cancelled, and a cancelled branch is the plan working.

cues.text: Take your last ten trades against a range extreme on your list. Score each trade a point for each line that is true.
One: branch. It came from a branch written before 9:25 that named this zone and this read.
Two: two closes. At least two 1-minute closes printed beyond the far edge before the reclaim.
Three: reclaim. A 1-minute close back beyond the near edge printed before any order.
Four: trigger. A Pause N Go fired from the reclaimed zone, and the entry was the resumption close.
Five: stop. It rested behind the far edge from the moment of entry.
Six: confirmation. Trapped Traders was recorded only with all three boxes ticked, and size did not change because of it.
Six of six is the trade this page teaches. Lines one and four override the score.
A trade at a range extreme that misses either one was a fade with no entry behind it, however well it scored. A fade with no entry is a hope with an order ticket.
If two or more of your ten miss line one or four, the fix goes on your sheet for the next session: every range-extreme zone carries a branch number or the word nothing.
If none miss them, find the line from two, three, five and six that the most trades missed. If three or more missed it, it becomes a written check on your pre-market sheet.
Getting it wrong is scoring the trades you remember. Score only what is on the paper.
Next session, the first time price touches a range extreme on your sheet, write the window's end time beside the zone on the chart.
At that time, write one word next to it: accepted, rejected or neither. That is the whole assignment.
In one line: a level that fails is the same test as a level that holds, with the other answer.
It cancels or ends a branch and sets your targets. It never hands you an order, except through two closes, a reclaim and a Pause N Go.
Where it goes next. Module 12, the gap setups, starts the reads from the other side, when the open is outside the prior day's range.
Module 13 teaches Pause N Go in full.
Module 14 turns the trigger into an order.
Module 15 is the plan, with the nothing case.
Modules 17 and 18 are the session mark-up and the journal.

check.q: Which two lines of the six-line score override the score?
check.why: Branch and trigger. A trade at a range extreme that misses either was a fade with no entry behind it.

check.q: Three of your ten trades missed line five, the stop. None missed lines one or four. What happens?
options: Line five becomes a written check on your sheet
check.why: If none miss lines one and four, the line missed by three or more trades becomes a written check on your pre-market sheet.

check.q: What is the assignment?
options: Write the window's end time at the first touch, then one word: accepted, rejected or neither
check.why: That is the whole assignment: the end time beside the zone, and one word at that time.

check.q: You score your last ten trades at a range extreme. Which trades count?
options: Only what is on the paper, from the journal
check.why: Getting it wrong is scoring the trades you remember. Score only what is on the paper.

options: A bar leaves a wick above the zone
The 15-minute window has passed with no 5-minute close beyond the far edge and price is back on the range side
The first 5-minute bar closes inside the zone
questions.why: Only after the window has passed, with no 5-minute close beyond the far edge and price back on the range side.

questions.q: What does a rejection never do?
questions.why: It cancels a branch, ends a branch or sets a target. It never places an order.

questions.q: A failed breakout above a zone is…
options: Two 5-minute closes above, then a 5-minute close below
Two 1-minute closes above the far edge, then a 1-minute close back below the near edge
questions.why: Mirror of the failed breakdown: two 1-minute closes beyond the far edge, then a 1-minute close back beyond the near edge.

options: Part of the read, not the trigger
questions.why: The reclaim is part of the read. The entry is the Pause N Go from the reclaimed zone.

questions.q: What is the invalidation of the failed breakdown branch in the example?
options: A 5-minute close below the far edge, before or after the reclaim
A 1-minute close at the near edge
questions.why: A 5-minute close beyond the far edge ends the branch for this test, and no reclaim after it switches it back on.

questions.q: Trapped Traders printed on your failed breakdown. What changes on the ticket?
options: Nothing: it adds a word to the confirmation field
questions.why: A confirmation never changes size or any number on the ticket.

questions.q: Before 9:25, a range-extreme zone with no branch carries…
options: The word nothing, and no order
questions.why: Every range-extreme zone carries a branch number or the word nothing.

questions.q: In Case 1 the stop is 12 points and the target 54. Which is true?
options: The trade clears 2 to 1 at about 4.5 to 1
The stop sits inside the zone
questions.why: 54 divided by 12 is 4.5, so the trade clears the 2 to 1 check.
